items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: Robert D. Walker was a featured player in Handy's band.

ctx.x: Oh, there's Livery Stable. Livery Stable blues.

That was his, that was his big feature. And I would always call him out for that number. Yeah, he featured that and played it good too. And he had such strong, devilish lips. He didn't have the proper tone like Hatton had, Frank Hatton or Carl Travis or Robert Walker or Willie Triggs. See, I had ace trumpet players, good ones. They were very, very good. Willie Triggs was the outstanding trumpet player on the Georgia Misses before he came to the Army. And Robert D. Walker was a featured player in Handy's band. And…
